billpilot.heading: BillPilot
billpilot.pitch: An AI copilot for bill disputes and billing operations, built on a mock TM Forum-shaped telecom billing system — every customer, bill, and fault is synthetic.
billpilot.deckNote: This is the original design spec. Phases 1–5 were built largely as described; the final phase — testing — was reduced to basic pytest smoke tests, not a full end-to-end suite.

explainer.title: The problem
explainer.body: Telecom billing throws up disputes, treatment and entitlement mix-ups, and failures that often surface only after a customer complains. BillPilot is a role-based AI copilot over a mock billing system: a customer assistant that explains bills and policy with citations, a CSR console that investigates and proposes a fix, and an ops control tower that watches for failures and runs the reports — all backed by a human-approval queue for anything that touches money or service.

explainer.title: How it works
explainer.body: A FastAPI service exposes TMF-shaped routes (customer bill, usage, payment, product inventory, trouble ticket, and a TMF654-style balance) over a PostgreSQL ledger — the database is the system of record. The copilot is a tool-calling agent whose only way into billing data is that same HTTP API, called with the signed-in user's own session or API key, so it never queries the tables directly. Policy answers come from a small RAG index: docs/knowledge is embedded with pgvector and searched for citations. Guardrails keep the agent to read and advise — any credit, bar/unbar, or plan change is only proposed, and sits in an approval queue for a different role to apply. Every chat turn and every write lands in an audit log. The customer portal, CSR console, and ops control tower are one React + Vite + TypeScript app behind sign-in, with optional Langfuse tracing per turn, deployed as one Docker container plus a hosted Postgres — Render's free web service and Neon's free Postgres.

billpilot.dataNote: The ledger is a synthetic billing dataset generated with Faker — 500 customers across 6 months of history in a 23-table PostgreSQL schema — with common telecom issues (duplicate charges, missed discounts, failed payments, barring mistakes, and more) seeded in so the copilot and the rule-based checks have something real to find. No real customer, invoice, or vendor data is used anywhere.
billpilot.testingNote: Testing: ruff and pytest in CI for the backend, including a pytest smoke test for the eval harness (guardrail cases get refused, no case calls an approve tool, a report file is produced), plus a Vitest suite for the UI. That's smoke-level coverage, not a full end-to-end suite.

personas.body: Asks things like “Why is my bill higher this month?” and gets a line-by-line explanation with a policy citation it can open. Can also raise a dispute, which the CSR and ops queue picks up from there.

Searches an assigned account, works through Bills, Lines, Usage, Payments, Treatment, Tickets, and Disputes tabs, and asks the copilot for an explanation with its tool calls visible. Can propose a credit — it only ever proposes, never applies. A troubleshooting panel takes a pasted error and returns numbered steps cited from the runbooks.

Approves or rejects proposed credits (never the account's own proposer), watches the failure dashboard for stuck bill runs and failed events, generates billing and collections reports, runs rule-based fraud and revenue checks, and handles onboarding and bulk migration — including a dry run, a human sign-off, and rollback by batch.

phases.title: Phase 1 · Core ledger & APIs
phases.body: PostgreSQL ledger, a Faker-based synthetic generator, FastAPI routes shaped like TM Forum Open APIs, an approval queue and audit log, Docker Compose, and CI.

phases.title: Phase 2 · Copilot
phases.body: A tool-calling agent, a small RAG policy index with citations, guardrails, propose-not-apply for anything that moves money, and an eval harness.

phases.title: Phase 3 · Product surface
phases.body: The customer portal, CSR console, and ops control tower as one React + Vite + TypeScript app. Sign-in replaced the old persona switcher, with role and scope read from the database; a free-tier deploy; optional Langfuse tracing.

phases.title: Phase 4 · Operations layer
phases.body: A billing-event pipeline (a Postgres outbox, or Redpanda locally), a failure dashboard, SQL reports, rule-based fraud and revenue checks, and a CSR troubleshooting assistant.

phases.title: Phase 5 · Onboarding & migration
phases.body: One API call opens a new subscriber. A bulk legacy-file migration runs a dry run, needs a human sign-off, commits idempotently, and can roll back per batch.
